Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Ignatius Sancho (author, Wikidata Q1657368), died 1780; Joseph Jekyll (other, Wikidata Q6284370), died 1837. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Sancho, Ignatius, 1729-1780; Jekyll, Joseph, 1754-1837 [Contributor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Letters of the late Ignatius Sancho, an African. To which are prefixed, memoirs of his life.  1784, 1784, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/bim_eighteenth-century_letters-of-the-late-igna_sancho-ignatius_1784. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 75%, 53%, 100% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Joseph Jekyll, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
